inspection_summary: Inspected all 3,633 normalized lines of the thesis, including front matter, the zeta-function overview, the contour-based derivation of the Riemann-Siegel formula, the saddle-point approximation chain, Gram and Turing root-certification logic, the finite-height computation, implementation/domain analysis, all four code appendices, and the bibliography. The prose preserves the main semantic mechanisms despite degraded display mathematics; exact symbolic reuse of several contours, coefficient identities, and plotted examples requires the retained PDF. The appendices are readable enough to expose theory-to-code choices and an apparent gram/graham identifier inconsistency that should be scan-checked before being treated as an authorial code defect.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter, abstract, contents, and acknowledgements
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Identifies the survey/implementation goal, saddle-point efficiency claim, verification aim, and source organization; administrative and contents material is non-unit front matter.

sections_inspected.label: Chapter 1: Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Frames finite-height RH verification, contrasts Euler-Maclaurin with Riemann-Siegel complexity, and states the thesis as a derivation-and-implementation manual.

sections_inspected.label: Chapter 2: Overview of the Riemann Zeta Function
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds the Dirichlet/Euler-product starting representation, contour analytic continuation, functional symmetry, xi function, and the real-valued critical-line Z representation.

sections_inspected.label: Chapter 3.1-3.3: Formula and exact decomposition
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the Riemann-Siegel formula and transforms the global contour representation into a computable finite cosine sum plus an exact contour remainder.

sections_inspected.label: Chapter 3.4-3.9: Saddle point and successive approximations
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Chooses the saddle-adapted truncation, deforms and localizes the contour, normalizes variables, truncates a rapid series, extends the path, and compresses coefficient extraction through recurrences.

sections_inspected.label: Chapter 3.10-3.11: Example and errors
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Illustrates evaluation and separates contour-localization, series-truncation, and finite-precision errors, emphasizing sign certification rather than high-precision values.

sections_inspected.label: Chapter 4.1-4.2: Verification and Gram structure
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Turns critical-line evaluation into a root-counting heuristic, states Gram's Law and its failures, and packages exceptional intervals as Gram blocks.

sections_inspected.label: Chapter 4.3: Turing root-count certification
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Relates the argument-principle total N(T) to theta and S(T), derives parity at good Gram points, and uses correction-point staircases plus Turing's averaged bound to certify completeness.

sections_inspected.label: Chapter 5.1-5.2: Computed verification
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Reports the finite computation and instantiates the Turing inequality to turn a critical-line lower count into an exact all-strip count at the selected height.

sections_inspected.label: Chapter 5.3-5.5: Programs and effective domain
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Records computational provenance, symbolic coefficient preprocessing, staged accuracy, adaptive Gram-block search, Turing-adjustment search, and precision-driven validity limits.

sections_inspected.label: Chapter 6: Conclusion and future work
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Distinguishes single-value from batched evaluation bottlenecks and proposes approximating the main Dirichlet sum to enable extended-precision verification.

sections_inspected.label: Appendix A: C functions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Provides executable theta, Gram-point, coefficient, Z, and adaptive Gram-block routines; most coefficient literals repeat the earlier symbolic construction.

sections_inspected.label: Appendix B: Simple Z evaluator
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Provides a routine sampling driver around the reusable Z implementation.

sections_inspected.label: Appendix C: Root-counting program
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Implements Gram-law testing, precision escalation, Gram-block fallback, lower-bound accounting, and result reporting.

sections_inspected.label: Appendix D: Turing-adjustment program
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Implements the sign and monotonicity constraints on adjusted Gram points with step refinement.

sections_inspected.label: Bibliography
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Lists cited sources; no new source-supported mechanism is developed.

accepted_units.title: Riemann-Siegel trades generality for square-root-time critical-line evaluation
accepted_units.why_material: Contrasts the order-t Euler-Maclaurin route with a specialized square-root-time method and identifies floating-point precision as the eventual operational boundary.
accepted_units.context_note: Read with the thesis aim at lines 252-255; historical scale claims are contextual rather than independent validation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose is clear; the extracted square-root glyph is split across lines 249-250.

accepted_units.title: Dirichlet series and Euler product expose the sum-product bridge
accepted_units.why_material: Defines zeta in its convergent half-plane and connects the additive Dirichlet representation to multiplicative prime structure by geometric-series expansion.
accepted_units.context_note: Special-value remarks are ancillary; the representation change is the reusable content.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Displayed sums/products have degraded spacing but are recoverable from checked prose.

accepted_units.title: A deformable Hankel-type contour supplies a global zeta representation
accepted_units.why_material: Replaces the half-plane-limited series definition by a contour integral and explains why contour radius and offset can vary without changing the value.
accepted_units.context_note: Branch choice for log(-x) and avoidance of integrand singularities are essential setup.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Contour drawings are absent from extraction; branch and deformation semantics survive in prose, while exact geometry needs the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Mellin integration and monotone convergence recover the Dirichlet series
accepted_units.why_material: Shows how scaling the factorial integral, summing a finite geometric family, and passing the limit through the integral yields the Mellin identity for zeta.
accepted_units.context_note: The starting restriction is real s greater than one; later lines extend the result analytically.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula layout is degraded, but the substitution, monotonicity, and limiting argument are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Branch-side contour limits reproduce the Mellin identity
accepted_units.why_material: Decomposes the contour into upper, circular, and lower pieces, uses dominated convergence on the rays, discards the shrinking arc, and recombines the branch phases with the factorial reflection identity.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the proof bridge from the deformable contour to the ordinary zeta series in the initial domain.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several path drawings and epsilon glyphs are degraded; the proof mechanism is prose-recoverable, but exact displayed formulas require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Analyticity upgrades the contour identity to global continuation
accepted_units.why_material: Separates the convenient limiting contour from the equivalent finite contours and argues uniform convergence/analyticity to define zeta on the complex plane except its simple pole.
accepted_units.context_note: The observation about cancellation at positive integers is part of the extension logic, not a separate numerical claim.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose is clear; some displayed contour notation is formula-layer dependent.

accepted_units.title: Functional symmetry becomes the entire xi invariant
accepted_units.why_material: Repackages the functional equation into xi(s)=xi(1-s), removing zeta's pole and making reflection about the critical line explicit.
accepted_units.context_note: The trivial-zero observation is a consequence; the symmetry is the mechanism used later.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Displayed gamma-factor notation is partly degraded but the transformation and invariant are explicit.

accepted_units.title: Critical-line zeros become sign changes of a real Z function
accepted_units.why_material: Uses conjugation plus functional symmetry to make xi real on the critical line, then factors zeta by a phase so zero finding reduces to robust real sign changes.
accepted_units.context_note: The exact theta phase is later approximated by Stirling's series.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The phase formulas are visually degraded; the real-valuedness and sign-correspondence claims are clear in prose.

accepted_units.title: Riemann-Siegel is a short cosine sum with a systematic remainder expansion
accepted_units.why_material: States the operational formula, the saddle-scaled truncation index, the fractional parameter, the coefficient hierarchy, and a short asymptotic theta evaluation.
accepted_units.context_note: This statement is interpreted by the subsequent derivation and error analysis, not accepted as an unqualified exact identity.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Coefficient formulas are extraction-risky; the sum-plus-remainder architecture and scaling are recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Contour expansion produces dual finite sums and an exact remainder
accepted_units.why_material: Splits off N exponential terms, expands the contour across paired singularities, evaluates residues, and obtains a global representation comprising two finite sums plus a residual contour integral.
accepted_units.context_note: Cauchy deformation and conjugate residue pairing are necessary local setup; the positive-integer values are supplied by analytic continuation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Contour diagrams and residue displays are degraded, but the sequence of transformations is recoverable from prose and equation labels.

accepted_units.title: Functional symmetry collapses the exact representation to a cosine main sum plus contour remainder
accepted_units.why_material: Restricts to the critical line, applies the xi/phase normalization, pairs conjugate finite sums into cosines, and isolates the computable main sum SN from the remainder RN.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the exact starting decomposition before the approximation steps.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-heavy span; prose and labeled endpoints support the mechanism, while exact prefactors need the retained PDF.

accepted_units.title: The truncation index is chosen to align the contour with a saddle
accepted_units.why_material: Explains that N is determined by the approximation geometry, deforms the remainder contour through the near saddle, and uses steepest descent to concentrate mass on a short segment.
accepted_units.context_note: The numerical plot is illustrative only; the contour-deformation and saddle-selection argument is the semantic core.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Contour and surface plots are absent/degraded, but prose states the path pieces, saddle location, and concentration rationale.

accepted_units.title: Discarding off-saddle contour pieces has exponentially small error
accepted_units.why_material: Marks the first genuine approximation and attaches an explicit exponential bound to replacing the full deformed contour by its short saddle-crossing segment.
accepted_units.context_note: The cited bound is reported from Edwards rather than independently derived here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The approximation formula is readable with minor layout degradation.

accepted_units.title: Dominant saddle behavior is factored out before series expansion
accepted_units.why_material: Changes variables and separates the large exponential/quadratic contribution so the residual function has a rapidly convergent power series on the local path.
accepted_units.context_note: The precise coefficients are intentionally deferred; the normalization strategy is the reusable move.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact exponential factors are formula-layer dependent, while motivation and rapid-convergence claim are explicit.

accepted_units.title: Series truncation and path extension make the remainder termwise integrable
accepted_units.why_material: Identifies series truncation as the dominant error source, then extends the local path so the retained terms can be integrated and represented by coefficient-integral pairs.
accepted_units.context_note: The exact evaluation of the base integral is attributed to Riemann; error magnitude is analyzed later.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Path image and coefficient integrals need PDF checking for exact transcription; the staged approximation semantics are clear.

accepted_units.title: Recurrences extract remainder coefficients without computing every intermediate term
accepted_units.why_material: Uses degree structure, a generating relation, and recurrences to compute only the coefficient combinations needed at each asymptotic order, while noting direct symbolic computation as an alternative.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a labor-saving coefficient-compression method rather than a new error bound.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Many displayed recurrence symbols are extraction-risky; the polynomial-degree and dependency structure is recoverable from prose.

accepted_units.title: Verification reliability separates analytic truncation error from machine arithmetic error
accepted_units.why_material: Distinguishes off-saddle error, dominant series-truncation error, and accumulated floating-point phase/summation error, then reframes the required output as a certifiable sign rather than a highly precise value.
accepted_units.context_note: Reported constants and thresholds are cited results and architecture-specific observations.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose is clear; isolated big-O and sum formulas have mild extraction degradation.

accepted_units.title: Gram's Law is a productive empirical sign heuristic, not a theorem
accepted_units.why_material: Derives the expected alternation from phase behavior and a positive-real-part tendency, states the sign rule, records its finite and infinite failures, and explicitly limits it to empirical root-count guidance.
accepted_units.context_note: The plotted examples are illustrative; the key epistemic distinction is between plausible tendency and rigorous certification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Graph images are absent, but definitions, sign rule, failure statement, and caveat are clear.

accepted_units.title: Good/bad Gram points localize exceptions into Gram blocks
accepted_units.why_material: Clarifies that sign alternation gives only a lower bound and organizes consecutive failures into blocks that can be searched for the expected number of roots.
accepted_units.context_note: Completeness requires an independent upper/total-root bound developed next.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Plain prose and definitions are intact.

accepted_units.title: Argument-principle root totals expose Backlund's contour-certification bottleneck
accepted_units.why_material: Connects N(T) to a contour integral of xi'/xi and then to theta plus a zeta argument term, while showing why direct nearest-integer evaluation requires proving a nonvanishing contour condition each time.
accepted_units.context_note: The contour assumption is essential and is not silently discharged by the displayed formula.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Contour drawings are degraded; prose preserves the argument-principle role and the nonvanishing limitation.

accepted_units.title: Turing's averaged S bound combines with parity at good Gram points
accepted_units.why_material: Replaces repeated contour nonvanishing checks by an averaged bound for S, then proves S(gm) is even using critical-line sign parity and off-line zero pairing, reducing exactness to the inequality |S(gm)|<2.
accepted_units.context_note: The averaged inequality is cited from Turing's use of Littlewood's result; the parity derivation is shown locally.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula layout is degraded but the logical parity chain is readable.

accepted_units.title: Adjusted Gram-point staircases turn an averaged bound into a finite certificate
accepted_units.why_material: Constructs sign-corrected sample points, compares root and Gram counting staircases, integrates their discrepancy, and derives a computable upper bound whose satisfaction completes the root count.
accepted_units.context_note: The correction sequence must remain strictly increasing and its total displacement must stay small; these are certificate conditions, not tuning conveniences.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Staircase figures are absent from extraction, but their definitions and inequalities are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: A critical-line lower count plus Turing's upper bound yields an exact finite-height conclusion
accepted_units.why_material: Reports the found roots and correction data, evaluates the Turing inequality below two, and combines the resulting all-strip upper bound with the critical-line lower count to certify equality at the tested height.
accepted_units.context_note: This is source-reported finite computational evidence, not evidence for RH beyond the stated range; provenance and period hardware are given separately.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Tables and formulas are legible enough for the logical chain, though exact numeric reuse should be checked against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Implementation provenance exposes the cost and precision regime of the reported run
accepted_units.why_material: Records programs, compiler, machine, numeric types, optimization/readability tradeoffs, and wall-clock contrast between exhaustive root counting and the short Turing calculation.
accepted_units.context_note: These details support interpretation and reproducibility of the source-reported experiment; they do not validate the result independently.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Plain prose is intact.

accepted_units.title: Remainder functions are precompiled into high-precision Taylor coefficients
accepted_units.why_material: Maps the analytic coefficient functions to a normalized variable, differentiates symbolically, and truncates coefficient series by magnitude to obtain fast runtime evaluation.
accepted_units.context_note: The later literal coefficient tables instantiate this construction and need not be separate semantic units.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Displayed function notation is mildly degraded; the Maple preprocessing and truncation rule are clear.

accepted_units.title: Remainder depth is an explicit speed-versus-certainty control
accepted_units.why_material: Makes the number of retained remainder terms a runtime parameter because most sign decisions need only two terms while difficult cases justify the full expansion.
accepted_units.context_note: This policy is realized as staged fallback in the main program.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Plain prose is intact.

accepted_units.title: Asymptotic theta supplies a fast Newton initializer for Gram points
accepted_units.why_material: Derives a cheap scale-appropriate starting approximation from the theta asymptotic and uses Newton iteration for rapid Gram-point location.
accepted_units.context_note: The stated initializer is tailored to the tested height range and is not a universal bound.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The approximate formula is degraded in layout but the initialization logic and convergence observation are explicit.

accepted_units.title: Gram-block search refines partitions and escalates precision under an error margin
accepted_units.why_material: Combines bisection-like partition refinement, an expected-root target, two accuracy stages, a hard warning path, and sign tests separated from zero by a justified error tolerance.
accepted_units.context_note: Failure to find the expected roots triggers scrutiny rather than a false completeness claim.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Plain prose is intact; epsilon appears as a degraded glyph but is defined contextually.

accepted_units.title: The main counter routes ordinary intervals through Gram's Law and exceptional blocks through adaptive search
accepted_units.why_material: Composes Gram-point location, cheap sign tests, precision escalation, and block search into a lower-bound counting pipeline with explicit summary outputs.
accepted_units.context_note: Its completeness is supplied only after the separate Turing certificate.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Plain prose is intact.

accepted_units.title: Turing adjustments are found by directional stepping with refinement fallback
accepted_units.why_material: Operationalizes the sign-correction constraints near Gram points and refines the step partition if a required adjustment is not found.
accepted_units.context_note: The source reports that the selected twenty-point case succeeded at the initial step size.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Plain prose is intact.

accepted_units.title: Certified signs can be sound while the sampling process remains incomplete
accepted_units.why_material: Separates false-positive protection from false-negative risk, models how input representation and accumulated cosine error grow with height, and defines the practical endpoint by comparison with the analytic tolerance.
accepted_units.context_note: The numerical crossover is an implementation-specific estimate and the five-term tolerance was not separately established.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose is clear; big-O formulas are mildly degraded.

accepted_units.title: Batch acceleration does not remove the single-evaluation Dirichlet-sum bottleneck
accepted_units.why_material: Distinguishes precomputation-based multiple-evaluation speedups from single-point evaluation, isolates the main cosine/Dirichlet sum as the bottleneck, and proposes matching its approximation error to the Riemann-Siegel remainder.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a prospective research direction, not a demonstrated algorithm in the thesis.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The displayed real-part identity is formula-risky but recoverable from the surrounding prose.

accepted_units.title: The appendix Z routine directly composes phase, main sum, and selectable remainder
accepted_units.why_material: Provides a code-level mapping from the analytic decomposition to finite-precision evaluation, including modular phase reduction and selectable asymptotic depth.
accepted_units.context_note: Literal coefficient generation is defined earlier; this span is the runtime evaluator.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: C text is readable; exact compilation depends on the surrounding appendix declarations and should be checked against the original source file/PDF.

accepted_units.title: The Gram-block routine implements tolerance-gated multistage refinement and warning
accepted_units.why_material: Instantiates adaptive partition depth, sign margins, two remainder depths, and an explicit unresolved-block warning, exposing the source's executable notion of a certified found root.
accepted_units.context_note: The extracted code calls graham at lines 3080 and 3138 although the defined routine is gram; verify the PDF/source before classifying this as an original compile defect.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mostly readable C, but broken comment delimiters and the gram/graham mismatch may reflect source or extraction defects.

accepted_units.title: The root-counting program escalates difficult Gram points and delegates exceptional blocks
accepted_units.why_material: The program header states lower-bound semantics and uncertain-region warnings; the body implements cheap tests, precise fallback, block delegation, accounting, and progress/result reporting.
accepted_units.context_note: The code does not itself establish that all strip zeros were found; that conclusion requires the separate Turing stage.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: C extraction is readable enough for control flow; exact compilation was not performed and would require the full source environment.

accepted_units.title: The Turing program enforces sign and order constraints while shrinking its adjustment step
accepted_units.why_material: Implements construction of adjusted Gram samples, bidirectional search for sign-certified values, restart on loss of strict ordering, and output of the certificate data.
accepted_units.context_note: This executable search constructs inputs to the mathematical bound; it does not by itself prove the bound or verify the reported run.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: C extraction is largely readable, with formula comments and long lines subject to PDF text-layer risk.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From analytic continuation to a real, computable critical-line remainder problem
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The same contour representation that globally defines zeta is expanded across singularities, normalized by functional symmetry, and paired with its conjugate to turn a complex analytic object into a real cosine sum plus one localized remainder.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Several exact contour geometries and prefactors are formula-layer dependent and require the retained PDF for symbolic reuse.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The Riemann-Siegel approximation is a sequence of controlled representational compressions
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Saddle alignment concentrates the contour, dominant behavior is factored out, a rapid residual series is truncated, and recurrence structure compresses coefficient evaluation; the source then distinguishes the error introduced at each compression from machine error.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source cites rather than rederives the sharp error constants, and the extracted equations are insufficient for exact coefficient reconstruction without scan checking.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Heuristic localization and independent total-count certification have complementary roles
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Gram's empirical law cheaply supplies a critical-line lower count and localizes exceptions, while Turing's parity and averaged S bound independently cap the total strip count; equality of the bounds, not the heuristic alone, yields the finite verification.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The conclusion is finite-height and conditional on the reported numerical sign/error certificates; it is not evidence for all heights.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The executable pipeline encodes uncertainty through margins, escalation, and warnings
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Analytic error bounds become sign margins; ambiguous evaluations trigger more remainder terms, deeper partitions, or explicit warnings; Turing adjustments are constructed separately to certify completeness.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The appendix was inspected textually but not compiled, and the extracted gram/graham mismatch plus broken comments require original-source verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Precision and throughput bottlenecks determine the meaningful verification frontier
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Square-root analytic complexity enables large searches, but phase representation and accumulated summation error eventually dominate; batching accelerates many nearby evaluations while single-value evaluation retains the main Dirichlet-sum bottleneck.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: All crossover scales are tied to the thesis's late-1990s implementation, numeric types, and reported architectures.

stop_reason: All 3,633 lines were inspected and exactly partitioned. Every distinct source-supported mechanism in the analytic derivation, approximation/error chain, Gram-Turing certification, finite computation, domain analysis, and executable control flow is represented; the unselected remainder consists of front matter, plots/examples that repeat selected mechanisms, literal coefficient tables, simple wrapper code, page scaffolding, and bibliography. Further segmentation would predominantly duplicate these mechanisms or promote formula/code text that first requires original-artifact verification.
